verified_facts.text: The hotel is on Lexington Avenue in Midtown East, one block from Grand Central Terminal.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Benjamin Royal Sonesta is located on Lexington Avenue in Midtown East, one block from Grand Central Terminal

verified_facts.text: The hotel is within walking distance of Fifth Avenue, Rockefeller Center and the Theater District.
verified_facts.excerpt: within walking distance of Fifth Avenue, Rockefeller Center, and the Theater District. It’s the quieter, more residential side of Midtown.

verified_facts.text: Architect Emery Roth completed the hotel's 26-story Lexington Avenue building in 1927, designed to feel more like a Manhattan residence than a commercial tower.
verified_facts.excerpt: In 1927, architect Emery Roth completed a 26-story building on Lexington Avenue designed to feel more like a Manhattan residence than a commercial tower.

verified_facts.text: Georgia O'Keeffe captured the building's silhouette in her painting New York Night.
verified_facts.excerpt: A year later, Georgia O’Keeffe captured its silhouette in New York Night, one of her most celebrated works.

verified_facts.text: The building became an official New York City landmark in 2017.
verified_facts.excerpt: becoming an official New York City landmark in 2017

verified_facts.text: The Neo-Romanesque building is one of the most recognized works of architect Emery Roth.
verified_facts.excerpt: the Neo-Romanesque edifice exuded the ambience of a private club and is one of the most recognized works by famed architect Emery Roth

verified_facts.text: The hotel completed a full renovation of the lobby and all guestrooms and suites in 2024 with design firm DLR Group.
verified_facts.excerpt: The hotel completed a full renovation in 2024 of the lobby, Sonesta Work Suite and all guestrooms and suites in partnership with design firm DLR Group

verified_facts.text: The 2024 renovation drew on two design inspirations: Benjamin, in bold architectural details, and Beverly, the building's original 1927 name, in softer gilded curves.
verified_facts.excerpt: around two design inspirations: Benjamin, represented in bold architectural details, and Beverly, the building’s original 1927 name rendered in softer, gilded curves

verified_facts.text: The hotel's mascot, Oscar, The King of New York, is drawn from the original building facade.
verified_facts.excerpt: The hotel’s mascot, Oscar, The King of New York, is drawn from the original building facade.

verified_facts.text: Custom artwork with an ode to New York City is integrated throughout the guest rooms and suites.
verified_facts.excerpt: Custom artwork with an ode to New York City is integrated throughout the luxurious guest rooms and suites.

verified_facts.text: Because the building was originally designed as apartments, the guest rooms are larger than standard Manhattan hotel rooms.
verified_facts.excerpt: Because the building was originally designed as apartments by architect Emery Roth in 1927, the guest rooms are genuinely larger than standard Manhattan hotel rooms.

verified_facts.text: Guest Rooms feature herringbone wood floors, custom work desks and a kitchenette.
verified_facts.excerpt: feature modern amenities, herringbone wood floors, custom work desks, and a kitchenette

verified_facts.text: Balcony Suites have a private balcony over Midtown Manhattan overlooking New York landmarks, plus a separate living area and a kitchenette.
verified_facts.excerpt: A private balcony over Midtown Manhattan overlooking New York landmarks. Enjoy a separate living area, and a kitchenette.

verified_facts.text: Terrace Suites have private furnished terraces that overlook the city, with a separate bedroom, living area and kitchenette.
verified_facts.excerpt: with private furnished terraces that overlook the city. A separate bedroom, generous living area, and kitchenette

verified_facts.text: The Beverly Penthouse has a private outdoor corner terrace with views of the Manhattan skyline.
verified_facts.excerpt: private outdoor corner terrace seating with views of the Manhattan Skyline

verified_facts.text: The Benjamin Penthouse has a private Juliette balcony and a separate terrace with outdoor seating 22 floors above the Manhattan skyline.
verified_facts.excerpt: private Juliette balcony and separate terrace with outdoor seating offering views 22 floors above the Manhattan skyline

verified_facts.text: Guests can book full-floor stays on the upper floors, with penthouses and contiguous guestrooms.
verified_facts.excerpt: With expansive penthouses and contiguous guestrooms, our full-floor stays provide the space, service, and stature your milestone occasion deserves.

verified_facts.text: The Rest & Renew sleep program is the hotel's signature in-room wellness experience.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Rest & Renew Sleep Program is The Benjamin Royal Sonesta’s signature in-room wellness experience

verified_facts.text: Rest & Renew sleep amenities include a meditation cushion, a Loftie alarm clock and night light, a Nodpod weighted blanket and on-demand meditations.
verified_facts.excerpt: along with a meditation cushion, Loftie Alarm Clock, Loftie Night Light, Nodpod Body Weighted Blanket, and complimentary on-demand meditations

verified_facts.text: A one-on-one sleep consultant program is available.
verified_facts.excerpt: a one-on-one sleep consultant program is available

verified_facts.text: Every room comes with a curated physical book through the hotel's partnership with Bedside Reading.
verified_facts.excerpt: Every room comes with a curated physical title through The Benjamin’s partnership with Bedside Reading

verified_facts.text: The Kids Sleep Program was developed with sleep expert Dr. Rebecca Robbins.
verified_facts.excerpt: the Kids Sleep Program, developed with sleep expert Dr. Rebecca Robbins for younger guests

verified_facts.text: The kids sleep program provides a goose down kids pillow, a personalized sleep mask and wind-down tips in the room.
verified_facts.excerpt: Goose down kids pillow, personalized sleep mask, and a curated set of wind-down tips waiting in the room.

verified_facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the spa delivers serious bodywork along with an impressive menu of therapies.
verified_facts.excerpt: The spa delivers serious bodywork along with an impressive menu of therapies

verified_facts.text: The fitness center has treadmills, elliptical trainers, exercise bikes, a Peloton bike, yoga mats and free weights.
verified_facts.excerpt: We provide treadmills, elliptical trainers, exercise bikes, a Peloton bike, yoga mats and free weights for guest use.

verified_facts.text: Pets are welcomed through the PAWS program, with a welcome letter and complimentary dog treats at check-in.
verified_facts.excerpt: When you and your pet check in, we’ll greet you with a PAWS Welcome Letter and complimentary dog treats.

verified_facts.text: At The Parliament, Chef Rakmin Lee cooks modern American food with Korean, French and Italian threads.
verified_facts.excerpt: Chef Rakmin Lee cooks modern American with Korean, French, and Italian threads running through it.

verified_facts.text: The Parliament has its own entrance on Lexington, red leather banquettes and owl-shaped motifs.
verified_facts.excerpt: With its own entrance on Lexington, red leather banquettes, and owl-shaped motifs throughout, it's a proper destination of its own.

verified_facts.text: Guests who prefer a quieter room are encouraged to request an interior-facing room or a higher floor when booking.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guests who prefer a quieter room are encouraged to request an interior-facing room or a higher floor at the time of booking

verified_facts.text: Some rooms face an active city street on Lexington Avenue.
verified_facts.excerpt: like most Midtown Manhattan hotels, some rooms face an active city street

verified_facts.text: A Hotel Facilities Fee is charged per room, per night.
verified_facts.excerpt: Our Hotel Facilities Fee is $45 plus tax per room, per night

verified_facts.text: Guests must be 21 or older to check in.
verified_facts.excerpt: Guest must be 21 years or older to check in.

verified_facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says the hotel is family friendly, with connecting rooms, cribs and a kids sleep program.
verified_facts.excerpt: Yes, with connecting rooms, cribs, and a kids sleep program.

verified_facts.text: Conde Nast Traveler says Fifth Avenue, St. Patrick's Cathedral and Rockefeller Center are a 10-minute walk away.
verified_facts.excerpt: Fifth Avenue, St. Patrick's Cathedral, and Rockefeller Center are a 10-minute walk
